Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Chromatin accessibility memory after transient stimulus (ATAC-seq time course)
ideas.description: Stimulate cells (e.g., with TNF, wounding, or growth factor), then wash out and profile ATAC-seq and AP-1 (FOS/JUN) CUT&RUN at days to weeks. Persistent accessibility at AP-1 motif sites after AP-1 binding has decayed would show AP-1 'opens' chromatin that is remembered, as in the 'reedbird' wordlist-like persistent marks (e.g., 'crackled' enhancer scars). Like a 'printed' imprint that remains after the stamp is lifted.

ideas.title: Acute degron depletion to separate initiation from maintenance
ideas.description: Use auxin-inducible degradation of c-JUN/FOS or dominant-negative A-FOS at defined windows: during the stimulus only, or only after the memory is established. If depleting AP-1 during induction abolishes the later enhanced response but depleting it afterward does not, AP-1 is needed to write but not to maintain memory (and vice versa), testing whether AP-1 itself stores the state.

ideas.title: Secondary-challenge functional assay with single-cell readout
ideas.description: Prime cells with a first stimulus, rest them, then re-stimulate and measure transcription of AP-1 target genes by scRNA-seq or live reporters, comparing to naive cells. Faster or stronger responses in primed cells, with and without AP-1 perturbation, quantify memory, and single-cell data reveal whether it is a graded or bistable, heritable state across cell divisions.

ideas.title: Pioneer-like binding and histone mark dynamics at AP-1 sites
ideas.description: Track H3K27ac, H3K4me1, and BAF/SWI-SNF (BRG1) occupancy with CUT&Tag over time at primed AP-1 sites, and test with AP-1 motif mutation via CRISPR base editing or dCas9 interference at selected enhancers. Mark persistence that requires the motif and recruited remodelers would show a mechanistic route from transient AP-1 binding to a lasting epigenetic state.

ideas.title: Mathematical modeling and optogenetic perturbation of AP-1 dynamics
ideas.description: Control AP-1 activity with optogenetic or chemically induced pulses of varied duration and frequency, measure the resulting target gene state at later times, and fit ODE models of positive feedback (FOS/JUN autoregulation) versus chromatin-based memory. Model comparison, such as hysteresis and dependence on pulse number, discriminates network-based memory from epigenetic memory.
